# September 15 guidance review

Standard initial-noise optimization is integrated and functionally verified.
It substantially improves predicted goal accuracy. Reliable physical picking
and released placing remain unresolved. All scheduled priority GPU runs finished
at10:24a.m. Eastern. The artifact audit and handoff are complete for the11a.m.
review; both report observers are stopped and the results are frozen.

Start with `validation/guidance_noise_2026-09-15/review_11am/index.html`.
The four-panel `qualified_control_report_v1/recorded_vs_guided_8270.gif` is the
clearest visual: a recorded lift replays with the fixed controller, while a
generated lift from the same observed scene leaves the object on the table.
The recorded reference is not a generated success or the requested task target.
The validation directory is local and ignored by Git; it is not in a fresh clone.

## What is verified, and what remains a limitation

- Production sampler parity, replayed routing randomness, hidden-action/future
  independence, zero-update behavior, finite gradients through multiple windows,
  and real-checkpoint update behavior have dedicated receipts.
- Persistent physics state, including solver warmstart, survives chunking and
  restoration bitwise on16 recorded scenes at both steps. The object is never
  commanded. Twelve completed feedback-pair comparisons verify shared noise and
  the appropriate identical control trajectories. Candidate zero and the model
  selection reproduce their driver executions bitwise.
- CUDA backward accumulation is not bitwise by default. The first can feedback
  budget prefix differs by at most0.000090mm in its logged target distance;
  the stricter bitwise trace assertion fails and is reported as such. See
  [gradient repeatability](GRADIENT_REPEATABILITY_2026-09-15.md).
- The independent floating-hand MuJoCo controller qualifies11/16 recorded
  scenes. Collision, inertia, support height and motor-command conversion are
  approximations. Fine-step feedback results replay the same realized commands;
  they do not independently replan from finer-step observations. These are not
  robot or source-PhysX success rates.
- Recorded-task semantics differ from the primary precise held-point/released-
  place request. The task/reference and placing-release studies retain this
  distinction and all original thresholds. See [task semantics](TASK_SEMANTICS_2026-09-15.md).

Standalone H36 six-update runs use1512 model calls and about140seconds median;
24-update runs use5400 calls and about532seconds. Peak allocated GPU memory is
7.64–7.65GB. The two24-update prefixes are excluded from these runtime summaries.
Repeated24-update feedback uses11424 calls and about1130seconds planning time,
including the fresh-sampling control. Late best-of49 and24-update optimization
share3400 forward invocations including recomputation, but not backward FLOPs
or wall time. These uncompiled FP32 diagnostics do not establish real-time control.

## Recommended next work

1. Qualify the actual source-simulator motor-command interface on recorded and
   generated grasps. Resolve achieved finger opening versus motor targets before
   attributing every execution discrepancy to the world model.
2. Test contact/actuation consistency of short committed segments. Geometry-only
   guidance can arrange a predicted object and gripper together without ensuring
   the actual object follows. The new per-replan prediction plots localize that
   mismatch. More penalties alone are not yet an established solution.
3. Verify training support for the exact requested completion event, especially
   released placing. The current49-sample bowl bank never offers a released
   ending. A broader independently selected task/data audit is more informative
   than presenting a held object near the target as a successful place.
4. Freeze a fresh confirmation set before assessing further tuned methods.
   The current guidance-reserved cases have now been inspected and diagnosed;
   they remain useful regressions, but should not be relabeled as untouched
   confirmation data for changes designed from these findings.

Optional longer AL tails, additional seeds, and unimplemented steering methods
were deferred within the deadline. No new training, checkpoint comparison or
source-PhysX execution was launched. The Isaac license question remains pending.
Changes were committed locally; nothing was pushed. Unrelated collection work
in the shared checkout was left untouched.
